name: Split button
summary: A main action joined to a button that opens a menu of related actions.
description:
Use a split button when one action is the usual choice and a few close variants are needed now and then: save, save as copy, save and publish. The main button does the usual thing in one click; the arrow opens the rest.

It is two .v-btn elements and a .v-menu inside .v-split. The menu is the ordinary dropdown menu, so it opens without JS and data-v-menu adds the keyboard behaviour.

classes.name: v-split
classes.description: The wrapper. Joins the first two .v-btn children; the .v-menu after them is not part of the join.

classes.name: v-menu-end
classes.description: On the menu: lines it up with the end edge of the arrow button. It flips to the start edge when there is no room.

states.description: On the arrow button, with popovertarget pointing at the menu.
On the arrow button: name what it opens, such as "More save options". It has only an icon.

hooks.name: data-v-menu
hooks.description: Focus on open, arrow keys, typeahead, checkable items and focus return, as for any dropdown menu.

keyboard.action: On the main button, runs the main action. On the arrow button, opens the menu.
On the arrow button, opens the menu on the first or last item.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the arrow button.

a11y: The two buttons are separate Tab stops with their own names, so a screen reader hears the main action and the menu button apart.
The arrow button needs an aria-label that says what the menu holds, not just "More".
Put the most common action on the main button; the menu is for the variants.

examples.title: Save and merge
examples.description: A primary split button with a plain menu, and a secondary one whose menu picks a merge method.
